summary: This document provides clarifications, corrections, and updates to the TRILL base protocol, which gives least-cost forwarding in multi-hop networks, safe forwarding during temporary loops, and multipathing. It was replaced by RFC 7780.

eli5.summary: A rulebook had unclear and wrong parts. This fixes them. It has since been replaced by RFC 7780.

questions: what does rfc 7180 change in rfc 6325
how does trill handle overloaded switches
subtitle: Fixes, clarifications and small additions for the TRILL base protocol, from overloaded switches to MTU rules.

tldr.problem: After the TRILL base protocol was published in July 2011, development revealed errata in RFC 6325 and cases that needed clarification or updates.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC gathers the corrections: rules for overloaded RBridges, distribution tree fixes, nickname selection, MTU handling, port modes, the CFI/DEI bit, graceful restart and Hello reduction.
tldr.outcome: Where it conflicts with RFC 6325, RFC 6327 or RFC 6439, this document takes precedence, but it was itself replaced by RFC 7780.

today: RFC 7180 is a Proposed Standard that has been obsoleted by RFC 7780, which carries these fixes forward. It updated RFC 6325, RFC 6327 and RFC 6439.

sections.title: Purpose and Precedence
sections.content:
TRILL (Transparent Interconnection of Lots of Links) forwards frames across multi-hop networks using IS-IS link-state routing and a header with a hop count. Active development revealed five errors in the base specification, RFC 6325, plus cases needing clarification. RFC 6327 and RFC 6439 had already clarified adjacency and Appointed Forwarders.

If this document conflicts with any of those three, it takes precedence. It also updates the precedence ordering of RFC 6325 sections to 4 > 3 > 7 > 5 > 2 > 6 > 1. The change in the numbering of distribution trees is not backward compatible, and the errata fixes may not be compatible with implementations that followed the errors.
sections.eli5: When the fix list and the old rulebook disagree, follow the fix list. A couple of fixes mean old and new players must not mix.

sections.title: Overloaded and Unreachable RBridges
sections.content:
An RBridge sets the IS-IS overload flag when it cannot hold the whole link-state database, or when an operator configures it, for example during maintenance. Frames are not least-cost routed through an overloaded switch, though they may start or end there. An RBridge reachable only through overloaded switches or links with cost 2**24 - 1 is called data unreachable.

An overloaded RBridge cannot be trusted to compute distribution trees or do the reverse-path forwarding check, so it can only be a leaf. Other RBridges MUST ignore nicknames held by overloaded or data unreachable switches when choosing tree roots. On receiving a unicast frame it is not the egress for, an overloaded RBridge MUST NOT discard it for an unknown egress and MUST try another non-overloaded neighbor. It MUST NOT apply a reverse-path check to multi-destination frames and MUST NOT forward them.

To originate multi-destination frames, an overloaded RB2 uses OOMF (Overload Originated Multi-destination Frame) service from a non-overloaded neighbor RB3 that advertises it in its Hellos. RB2 tunnels the frame to RB3 with M bit 0, Hop Count 2, its own ingress nickname and the special OOMF egress nickname. RB3 turns it into a normal tree frame and MAY rate limit the service. Without such a neighbor, RB2 distributes the frame locally where it is Appointed Forwarder. It MUST NOT distribute locally when it tunnels, to avoid delivering twice.
sections.eli5: An overloaded switch is like a tired helper who can still carry their own bags but should not direct traffic. A rested neighbor takes the messages and sends them on for them.

sections.title: Distribution Trees and Nicknames
sections.content:
Several corrections concern distribution trees. The text on the number of trees in RFC 6325 is fixed to read "up to k if j is zero or the minimum of (j, k) if j is non-zero". Parent choice now MUST be (j-1) mod p instead of j mod p, so tree 1 picks parent 0. All RBridges must compute trees the same way or the reverse-path check will drop many frames. Costs must be taken from the tree root R to N, not from N to R. Switches MAY prune trees by actual IPv4 or IPv6 multicast address.

For nicknames, a conflict is won by the numerically higher priority, then by the higher seven-byte IS-IS ID. Nicknames of IS-IS unreachable switches MUST be ignored when checking for conflicts, but those of reachable ones MUST NOT be. An RBridge MUST keep monitoring for conflicts even when overloaded. If all valid nicknames (0x0001 through 0xFFBF) are taken, it can still act as a transit switch, but not as ingress, egress or tree root.
sections.eli5: Everyone must pick the same way to draw the family tree of paths, or messages get lost. Names are first come first served, and ties go to the higher number.

sections.title: MTU, Port Modes and the CFI/DEI Bit
sections.content:
The campus-wide size Sz is the minimum originatingL1LSPBufferSize across RBridges, but not less than 1470. TRILL's default is 1470 bytes, which leaves 27 bytes of headroom compared with classic Ethernet. TRILL Hello PDUs MUST NOT exceed 1470 bytes. Three errata are fixed: multicast MTU-probe and MTU-ack PDUs MUST go to the All-IS-IS-RBridges address, they MAY be unicast, and the MTU test compares X with Sz as greater than or equal.

A table spells out what each combination of the four port mode bits permits. The Disable bit normally disables all frames. Separately, because IEEE 802.1Q-2011 turned the CFI bit into a Drop Eligibility Indicator, the bit in the Inner.VLAN MUST now carry the DEI value from the EISS interface, and mixed old and new ports may corrupt data.
sections.eli5: The rules about how big a message can be and which kinds of messages each doorway lets through are spelled out more clearly.

sections.title: Hello Reduction and Appointed Forwarders
sections.content:
Switches SHOULD support graceful restart from RFC 5306. RFC 6327 is updated so that Hellos on a port must match in the PORT-TRILL-VER sub-TLV, whose five bytes are tracked per neighbor.

An optional Hello reduction lets switches send Hellos on fewer VLANs, but they MUST still always attempt to send in the Designated VLAN. To keep VLAN inhibition timers safe, an RBridge MAY use a self-appointing Appointed Forwarders sub-TLV or the new VLANs Appointed sub-TLV. A receiver sets each listed VLAN timer to the maximum of its current value and the Hello Holding Time.

The Designated RBridge SHOULD NOT appoint an overloaded RBridge as Appointed Forwarder unless there is no alternative, and SHOULD reassign VLANs from one that becomes overloaded.
sections.eli5: Switches can chatter less when they are sure of their neighbors, but they still shout in the main room. The boss avoids choosing a tired helper as a leader when another is free.

sections.title: IANA and Security
sections.content:
Three IANA actions are listed. Nickname 0xFFC1 is allocated as the egress nickname for an OOMF. Bit 1 of the per-neighbor Neighbor RECORD in the TRILL Neighbor TLV means "Offering OOMF service". Bit 0 of the PORT-TRILL-VER capability bits means "Hello reduction support".

The security section says the memo improves documentation and corrects five errata in RFC 6325, and does not change the security considerations of the RFCs it updates.
